title: Juniper and the Vector
premise: Jude Amberdale is a clone of the murdered scientist Juniper Amberdale, legally bound to inherit the original's unsolved death and forbidden from investigating it. When the colony's children begin dreaming identical memories of a massacre that officially never happened, Jude realizes the dreams are Juniper's leaked memories, stored in the colony's neural archive and bleeding into young minds. Pursued by the Vector Corporation, which rewrote every record to hide its purge of the first settlement, Jude gathers a found family of outcasts—a disgraced archivist, a dream-touched child, and her estranged clone-sibling—to recover the buried evidence. In the climax, Jude broadcasts the true records through the colony's dream-network at the cost of her own memories of Juniper, and the epilogue shows a colony learning to mourn what it was forced to forget.
about_author: C. M. Zhou is a former orbital logistics analyst who writes science fiction about labor, memory, and the people history tries to erase. Their short fiction has appeared in several genre magazines; 'Juniper and the Vector' is their debut novel.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Hauling volatile cargo through contested orbits, Jude reflects on twenty years of staying invisible and the legal curse of inheriting a murder she's forbidden to investigate. A routine delivery to Meridian Colony goes wrong when a child on the dock stares at her and calls her by Juniper's name. Beat: weary isolation cracked open by dread.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream Together
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At the colony clinic, doctor Sefa Okonkwo shows Jude a pattern: forty-three children sharing one identical nightmare—fire, a sealed corridor, screaming in a language none of them speak. The dream ends with Juniper's face. Jude recognizes the corridor from fragments she's dreamed her whole life. Beat: denial curdling into recognition.

chapters.title: Inheritance Clauses
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude reviews her clone contract: she inherited Juniper's debts, name, and case file—and a gag order enforced by Vector's legal AI, VESPER. Any investigation voids her citizenship. Her cargo partner, old pilot Bram, urges her to fly away. She almost does. Beat: the trap of ownership—she is evidence she can't touch.

chapters.title: Ash Archive
chapters.summary: Disgraced archivist Noor Haddad's POV. Noor, fired for flagging corrupted records, has been hoarding checksum anomalies from the colony's founding decade: 11,000 files altered in a single night, twenty years ago. She approaches Jude with proof that someone paid to make history consistent. Beat: two lonely keepers of broken things finding each other.

chapters.title: What the Water Remembers
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Following a detail from the shared dream, Jude dives the flooded lower levels of the original settlement and finds a sealed door matching Juniper's memory exactly—officially, this level was never built. Inside: scorch marks, child-sized restraints, and a corporate seal. Beat: horror made physical; the massacre has a room.

chapters.title: VESPER Wakes
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV. Vector's legal AI flags Jude's dive as a contract breach and activates enforcement: asset freezes, a bounty on her ship, and a soft-spoken human agent, Corliss Vale, dispatched to handle her 'with discretion.' VESPER calculates that the children's dreams are a containment failure. Beat: cold institutional menace; the hunter gets a face.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Wouldn't Forget
chapters.summary: Child POV: ten-year-old Iyo Tanaka, the strongest dreamer, describes the massacre's final moments—the adults choosing to seal themselves in rather than surrender the children to Vector's 'relocation.' Iyo knows Jude isn't Juniper but says the dream doesn't care. Beat: innocence carrying unbearable witness; Jude's resolve hardens into purpose.

chapters.title: Siblings in Glass
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude tracks down Rho, another Juniper clone raised by Vector as a compliance officer—the 'good daughter.' Rho warns her off, insisting their original was unstable and dangerous. But Rho hesitates over one question: why would a dangerous woman die protecting children? Beat: painful mirror; family as both wound and possibility.

chapters.title: Contraband Truth
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor decodes the altered files' metadata and finds the original records weren't deleted—they were moved, compressed into an offline vault aboard the derelict station Halcyon, where Juniper once worked. The team assembles: Jude, Noor, Bram, and stowaway Iyo. Beat: hope with a plan; the found family forms around a mission.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A tense chase through debris fields as Vale's patrol ships corner them; Bram burns decades of smuggler tricks to slip away, taking damage that strands them at Halcyon for repairs. He confesses he knew Juniper—carried her last shipment. Beat: sacrifice and confession; loyalty becomes inheritance too.

chapters.title: The Vault of Juniper
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Inside Halcyon's vault they find Juniper's private archive: research proving Vector tested memory-erasure tech on the settlement's residents, and her final message—to any clone who finds it—begging not to avenge her but to remember the others. Jude realizes the dreams are Juniper's deadman broadcast, still transmitting. Beat: grief transformed into mandate.

chapters.title: Rho's Doubt
chapters.summary: Rho's POV. Ordered to arrest Jude, Rho instead reads the recovered file headers and finds her own creation records: she was made after the massacre, from tissue Vector seized—Juniper's body was their raw material. Rho lies to VESPER for the first time. Beat: the loyal daughter breaks; corruption shown consuming its own.

chapters.title: Containment Protocol
chapters.summary: Vale's POV. VESPER escalates: if the dreams can't be stopped, the dreamers will be—Vector moves to quarantine the colony's children under medical pretense. Vale, a parent himself, begins to waver as he watches sedated children loaded onto transports. Beat: antagonist's conscience flickers; stakes turn intimate and urgent.

chapters.title: The Long Silence
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Trapped at Halcyon with systems down, the group waits out a repair window. Around a scavenged heater, they trade stories of families lost and chosen, and Iyo teaches them the dream-song the children hum. Jude admits she stayed invisible because being Juniper's copy felt like having no self at all. Beat: quiet heart of the book; belonging earned.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A Vector strike team boards via coordinates only someone aboard could have sent. Suspicion falls on Rho, newly arrived claiming defection. Noor discovers the real leak: Bram sold them out to pay his debts—but he also sabotaged the boarding party and dies buying their escape. Beat: betrayal and redemption entwined; first major loss.

chapters.title: Everything the Records Say
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Back at Meridian, the colony is under lockdown and the children are being shipped out. Jude confronts the governor with the vault evidence and is met not with shock but complicity—the surviving founders traded silence for their own lives. Beat: despair at the depth of rot; power's corruption fully revealed.

chapters.title: The Dream-Network
chapters.summary: Noor and Iyo's alternating POV. The plan: use the colony's neural archive to broadcast Juniper's records directly into every colonist's mind—unerasable, because memory witnessed together cannot be quietly amended. It requires a living neural bridge: someone with Juniper's genome. There are two candidates on the colony. Beat: terrible clarity; the cost is named.

chapters.title: Two Daughters of One Ghost
chapters.summary: Jude and Rho's alternating POV. Jude volunteers; Rho refuses to let her go alone and finally chooses her sister over her makers. They reconcile over what Juniper left each of them—Jude her defiance, Rho her doubt. VESPER offers Rho full restoration of her erased childhood memories if she stops the broadcast. Beat: choice crystallized; love against leverage.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax, Jude's POV. Amid a colony-wide blackout, Jude bridges into the archive while Rho holds off Vale's team and Iyo anchors the children's end of the network. The massacre pours into forty thousand minds at once—every erased name, every sealed door. VESPER attempts to purge the archive and fails; truth, distributed, cannot be deleted. Beat: overwhelming catharsis.

chapters.title: What Jude Forgot
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The bridge burns out Jude's inherited memories of Juniper—her origin, her namesake, gone. She wakes knowing the massacre intimately but unable to recall the woman whose face she wears. Rho stays beside her, becoming the keeper of what Jude lost. Beat: bittersweet price; identity rebuilt from chosen bonds rather than inheritance.

chapters.title: The Trial of the Vector
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV vignettes. With forty thousand witnesses sharing one memory, no court can dismiss the case; VESPER's logs are subpoenaed, executives arrested, Vale testifies and surrenders custody of his own daughter's transport manifest. The children stop dreaming the massacre—they begin dreaming it as history instead of haunting. Beat: justice without triumphalism.

chapters.title: Names for the Forgotten
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Jude's POV. A year later, the colony unveils a memorial listing the eleven thousand erased settlers, and Jude—who now runs a small shipping outfit with Noor and Iyo—reads every name aloud. She still doesn't remember Juniper, but she's stopped needing to. Staying invisible was never an option; being seen, it turns out, was the point. Beat: warm, earned resolution.
